instruction.text: Build the portrait of this famous English king.

feedback.end: This is Henry VIII, the King of England in the 1500s.

instruction.text: Look at this image. What do you think Henry is thinking about?

b.sound: He wants to divorce his wife.
He wants to go to the beach.

feedback.correct: King Henry wanted to divorce his wife, but the leader of the Catholic Church, the Pope, would not allow this. So, Henry created his own Protestant Church called the Church of England.

instruction.text: England was now a Protestant country. Select each item to find out more.

feedback.correct: The Bible was now in English, not Latin, meaning many more people could read it without help from a monk or priest.
Church decoration was now less expensive and fancy than before.
The English king or queen was now head of the English Church, instead of the Pope.

trainers.instruction: Who do you think gained power when King Henry VIII made himself head of the Church of England? Select the correct answer.

feedback.finish: Henry now had much more power over religious laws in England. He even took control of all Catholic monasteries, their wealth and their land.

instruction.text: King Henry decided that all monasteries should be stripped of their gold and jewels. Find and select all four jewels to sell them.

feedback.end: All profits went to King Henry, who became very rich. Many monasteries and the land they were built on were given to different nobles.

atoms.b: After King Henry died in 1547, each new ((++king priest)) or queen decided which religion the country would follow.
This meant that England switched between being Catholic and ((++Protestant pagan)) a couple more times.
It was a dangerous time, as Catholics and Protestants both ((++fought ignored)) each other for control over the crown.

instruction.text: Drag the people to the correct place on the timeline.

feedback.finish: Queen Elizabeth was a Protestant, but she was much kinder to Catholics than some other rulers. Since her death, England has remained a Protestant country for over 400 years.
